The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has reported that it intercepted a drone launched by the Houthis towards Saudi Arabia’s Mecca region.
The drone was “intercepted and destroyed” on Friday morning, coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a social media post. It was also reported that a missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia was earlier brought down, as hostilities between the Riyadh-backed Yemen government and Iran-backed Houthis continue to escalate.
A Houthi spokesperson denied targeting the Muslim holy city or surrounding region, reiterating that the group’s cross-border attacks remain strictly focused on Saudi energy and military infrastructure.
The Saudi-led coalition has previously accused the Houthis of launching drones towards Islam’s two holiest cities: Mecca and Medina.
“Our operations target [Saudi] oil facilities and military bases, and there is no longer anyone in this world who believes these fabrications and lies propagated by the criminal Al Saud regime,” the Houthi spokesman wrote.
Escalating hostilities
The opposing claims come as hostilities continue with no sign of slowing, and humanitarian agencies warn of worsening conditions for civilians.
On Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s eastern region. It later said two ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital, Riyadh, were also intercepted and destroyed.
Al-Malki reported early on Friday that the coalition’s air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile that targeted western Saudi Arabia.
Media outlets affiliated with the Houthis reported later that coalition air attacks were targeting the Mahliyah district in Marib, Haifan in Taiz, and Huwaishan in al-Jawf in the country.
Al Jazeera Arabic’s Hadeel al-Yamani reported from Taiz that fighting along the front lines was persisting.
The governor of Taiz said the city was suffering heavy shelling, with residential neighbourhoods taking hits.
“Aircraft can be heard frequently over the city, which remains under a suffocating siege, with no medical supplies, water or fuel getting in,” al-Yamani reported.
“On the western front, there were intermittent clashes around dawn. The northern fronts were relatively calm, but still saw sporadic fighting. There has been a notable escalation in hostilities around Jabal Saber and Jabal Habashi,” he said.

articles.full_text:
Alkem Laboratories (NSE:ALKEM) disclosed on 30 October 2026 that the US Food and Drug Administration conducted an inspection of its active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing facility at Mandva between 26 and 30 October 2026, concluding the five-day inspection with no Form 483 observations issued.
Key Highlights
- The US FDA inspection at Alkem's Mandva API facility ran for five days, from 26 October 2026 to 30 October 2026, and was concluded without any Form 483 observation being issued to the company.
- A Form 483 is issued by the US FDA when investigators observe conditions that may constitute violations of the Food Drug and Cosmetic Act; the absence of such a notice indicates no such conditions were recorded at Mandva.
- Alkem Laboratories filed the regulatory update with both BSE and NSE on 30 October 2026, signed by Manish Narang, President Legal, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer.
- The Mandva facility is classified as an API manufacturing plant, supplying active pharmaceutical ingredients that serve as core inputs for finished dosage formulations.
About the Company
Alkem Laboratories Limited (NSE:ALKEM), headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, is a pharmaceutical company engaged in the development, manufacture, and marketing of branded generics, generic medicines, and nutraceuticals. The company operates across the Indian domestic market and exports to regulated markets including the United States, through multiple manufacturing facilities covering finished dosage forms and API production. It is listed on both BSE (scrip code 539523) and NSE under the ticker ALKEM, and ranks among the top ten pharmaceutical companies in the Indian domestic formulations market by sales.
Announcement in Detail
Alkem Laboratories informed its exchange filing, submitted under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, that the US FDA carried out an inspection of the company's API manufacturing facility situated at Mandva. The inspection spanned five consecutive working days, commencing on 26 October 2026 and concluding on 30 October 2026. At the end of the inspection, the US FDA did not issue a Form 483 to the company, signifying that no inspectional observations were recorded against the facility during this period.
Form 483 observations, when issued, typically list conditions that an investigator considers to be potential violations and can precede a Warning Letter if left unaddressed. The clean closure of this inspection means the Mandva API plant has cleared this cycle of US FDA scrutiny without any documented compliance deficiencies. The filing was authorised by Manish Narang in his capacity as President Legal, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of Alkem Laboratories Limited.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that a US FDA inspection closed without Form 483 observations is a meaningful regulatory outcome for a pharmaceutical company whose export revenues are linked to US market approvals. The filing shows that the Mandva API facility has maintained compliance standards sufficient to satisfy US FDA investigators during this inspection cycle, which is relevant to the uninterrupted supply of active ingredients used in regulated-market formulations.
Shareholders will observe that any future Warning Letter or import alert arising from an API facility could restrict product supply to the United States, so a clean inspection record reduces that near-term compliance risk for this facility. The disclosed terms of this announcement introduce no dilution, no change in shareholding, and no financial obligation for the company or its shareholders.
Sector / Market Context
India is the largest supplier of generic medicines to the United States by volume, according to data published by the US FDA and the Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (Pharmexcil). US FDA inspections of Indian API and formulation facilities have intensified over the past several years, with the agency resuming a full schedule of overseas inspections following the COVID-19 related pause. Regulatory compliance at API facilities is a recurring area of scrutiny for Indian pharmaceutical exporters, making clean inspection outcomes a closely watched indicator across the sector.

articles.title: Capital markets underused in Sri Lanka’s growth drive: SEC chief - Daily Mirror - Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Capital markets underused in Sri Lanka’s growth drive: SEC chief  Daily Mirror - Sri Lanka
articles.full_text:
| Prof. Hareendra Dissabandara Pic by Pradeep Pathirana | 
Sri Lanka must rethink how it finances economic expansion to pursue sustained growth of 7–9 percent, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman Senior Professor Hareendra Dissabandara said, arguing that government borrowing and bank lending alone cannot meet the country’s long-term investment needs.
Addressing the Capital Market Industry Forum on October 27, Dissabandara said economic stabilisation had laid the foundation for recovery, but the next challenge was to mobilise investment that raises productivity, builds competitive enterprises, expands exports and creates employment.
He described recent growth of approximately 4–5 percent as encouraging following the economic crisis, while arguing that Sri Lanka should aspire to a sustained trajectory of 7–9 percent, supported by improvements in productivity, competitiveness and investment.
“We cannot simply announce a higher growth target and expect the economy to achieve it,” he said.
Policymakers must first establish how much additional investment is required, identify sectors offering the greatest potential for productivity gains, value addition, exports and employment, and determine how that investment can be financed.
“We cannot sustainably achieve higher growth by depending excessively on Government borrowing. Nor should the banking sector alone be expected to provide every form of financing required by a modern, expanding economy.”
While banks remained essential for working capital, business operations and conventional lending, long-term productive investments required financing instruments suited to their duration and financial requirements, he said.
Dissabandara distinguished between economic rescue, recovery and sustainable growth, warning against treating progress in stabilisation as the completion of Sri Lanka’s economic adjustment.
Debt restructuring, the IMF-supported programme and fiscal and monetary reforms had provided an important foundation, he said, pointing to progress in fiscal consolidation, external finances, exchange-rate management and economic confidence.
“But we must understand that economic rescue is not the same as economic recovery, and economic recovery is certainly not the same as sustainable economic growth.”
Although maintaining macroeconomic stability and completing reforms remained necessary, he argued that the country’s ambitions must extend beyond managing existing obligations or depending indefinitely on external financial assistance.
Sri Lanka needed to generate its own productive capacity, attract investment and improve living standards, supported by financial discipline, institutional accountability and sound economic systems.
Dissabandara said Sri Lanka had insufficiently used its capital market throughout much of its post-Independence development, with financing discussions concentrating heavily on government borrowing, commercial banking and external debt.
The country already possessed a stock exchange, market intermediaries, investment management institutions and a regulatory framework through which long-term capital could be mobilised, he noted.
“The capital market is not merely a place where investors buy and sell shares. It is a mechanism for capital formation, resource mobilization and the allocation of savings towards productive investment.”
Equity financing could enable businesses to raise funds without the same fixed repayment obligations associated with conventional borrowing, while corporate debt markets could provide longer-term funding matched to companies’ requirements.
Collective investment schemes could give smaller savers access to diversified investments, while new financial products could direct funds towards infrastructure, sustainable energy, industrial development and entrepreneurship.
“What Sri Lanka needs today is not simply more money circulating within the economy. We need more capital being directed towards investments that create lasting economic value.”
Greater use of public markets could also strengthen corporate governance, transparency, financial reporting and investment discipline, he said. Businesses seeking public funds must demonstrate their credibility, financial performance and prospects, while investors assess where to allocate their savings.
He urged companies and entrepreneurs to show greater willingness to use capital market financing to expand productive activities.

Infrastructure initiatives include the demutualisation of the CSE, a central counterparty mechanism and the development of a multi-asset-class derivatives exchange. Other priorities include investor education, research and training, regulatory development, digital transformation and risk management.
Some initiatives could deliver benefits relatively quickly, while others required substantial institutional preparation, consultation, technological investment and legislative or regulatory development, he said.

Some companies faced pressure on operating costs and profitability, but he cautioned against interpreting a broad market decline as evidence that every listed business had become fundamentally weak.

articles.title: Microsoft, 1M1B and MeitY Startup Hub Launch Green Skills & Applied AI CoE in Gujarat - SMEStreet
articles.summary: Microsoft, 1M1B and MeitY Startup Hub Launch Green Skills & Applied AI CoE in Gujarat  SMEStreet
articles.full_text:
The Government of Gujarat, through the Gujarat Knowledge Society (GKS), along with 1M1B Foundation (One Million for One Billion), MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) and Microsoft, inaugurated the Green Skills & Applied AI Centre of Excellence (CoE) at L.D. College of Engineering, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad.
ADVERTISEMENT
The inauguration was attended by Shri Mukesh Kumar Sharma, Additional Chief Secretary, Higher & Technical Education, Government of Gujarat, Shri Dilip Kumar Rana, IAS, Commissioner, Higher & Technical Education and CEO, Knowledge Consortium of Gujarat; and Manav Subodh, Founder and Chief Mentor, 1M1B Foundation, Dr. Nilay N. Bhupatani, Principal, L.D. College of Engineering;, alongside other government and industry representatives and young changemakers on wednesday.
Advancing India’s AI Vision Through Future-Ready Skills
Aligned with Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) and technology for inclusive growth, the Centre aims to connect future-skills development with practical applications and emerging career opportunities.
ADVERTISEMENT
As Gujarat strengthens its position in green semiconductor manufacturing, electronics and advanced technologies, the CoE will help prepare young people for evolving industry needs. It is part of a three-year partnership between the Government of Gujarat, through GKS, and 1M1B Foundation, which aims to train and engage up to 3 lakh youth in applied AI, green skills, sustainability and emerging technologies.
Building Skills for Green Semiconductor Manufacturing
With semiconductor investments taking shape in Dholera and Sanand, Gujarat is emerging as an important centre for semiconductor manufacturing and the wider electronics value chain. The CoE will help young people understand how green semiconductor manufacturing can reduce environmental impact through more efficient use of energy and resources, responsible water management, waste reduction and sustainable production practices. It will also encourage youth to explore how applied AI and emerging technologies can support process optimisation, quality control, resource efficiency and more sustainable industrial operations.
ADVERTISEMENT
Alongside hands-on learning in Applied AI, Solar Energy, Electric Vehicles and Wind Energy, the initiative will introduce participants to eco-friendly practices relevant to semiconductor manufacturing. It will also promote industry engagement, including mentoring, internships and potential employment pathways with semiconductor and electronics companies. This approach aims to equip participants with practical capabilities relevant to Gujarat’s expanding technology and manufacturing ecosystem.
Leadership Perspectives
Dr. Pradyuman Ganubhai Vaja, Cabinet Minister for Higher and Technical Education, Government of Gujarat, said, “Gujarat has been at the forefront of India’s industrial growth, and with the state emerging as a key hub for semiconductor manufacturing, we must ensure sustainability remains central to our progress. The Green Skills & Applied AI Centre of Excellence will help equip our youth with future-ready skills to harness AI and green technologies, drive sustainable industrial practices and address real-world challenges. By bringing together innovation, skills and sustainability, Gujarat can lead the way towards a future that combines technological advancement with economic prosperity and environmental responsibility.”
Manju Dhasmana, Senior Director - Elevate CSR, Microsoft, said, “Microsoft is honored to support the Government of Gujarat’s vision of building an AI-forward and future-ready state. The Ahmedabad Centre of Excellence will help equip young people with practical capabilities in Applied AI and Green Skills, connecting learning with emerging opportunities across Gujarat’s green semiconductor, electronics and advanced technology ecosystem. As AI transforms industries and the nature of work, this Centre of Excellence closely aligns with Microsoft Elevate’s focus on AI + Jobs, helping young people build the skills and pathways they need to participate in this evolving economy.”
Manav Subodh, Founder and Chief Mentor, 1M1B Foundation, said, “Our partnership with the Government of Gujarat aims to prepare young people for opportunities emerging from the state’s growing green semiconductor and advanced technology ecosystem. By combining Applied AI, Green Skills and industry-linked learning, we hope to equip youth with practical capabilities to support innovation, sustainable manufacturing and the jobs of the future.”
Building a National Network of Centres of Excellence
The Ahmedabad CoE is one of the five Green Skills & Applied AI Centres of Excellence being established by 1M1B Foundation and Microsoft, in collaboration with MeitY Startup Hub. Following the launch of Centres in Bengaluru, Lucknow and Hyderabad, the fifth Centre is scheduled to launch in Noida next week. Together, the Centres aim to expand access to Applied AI, climate innovation and future-ready skills across India.
The national network aims to engage 100,000 young people in Applied AI and Green Skills by 2030, connecting learning with industry exposure and pathways to employment, internships and entrepreneurship.
Microsoft will support the Centres through AI technologies, digital learning resources, employee mentorship, innovation challenges and capacity-building under its CSR programme, while 1M1B Foundation will lead implementation and management.

articles.summary: India vows to protect farmers in US trade deal  www.irishsun.com
articles.full_text:
RT.com
                
30 Oct 2026, 13:41 GMT+10
            
New Delhi says sensitive agricultural interests will remain protected as Washington seeks greater access to the country's farm market
India will not compromise the interests of its farmers in the trade deal it is negotiating with the US, the federal trade minister has said, amid warnings and protest calls from powerful farm groups against cheaper American agricultural imports.
New Delhi and Washington announced a framework for an interim trade agreement in February, but the pact is yet to be signed. Negotiations have faced repeated delays over market access and tariffs, and unpredictability in US tariff policies.
"Not a single sensitive interest of our farmers or any stakeholder has been compromised," Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said at an industrial development conference in New Delhi on Thursday. He maintained that India would gain a strong competitive advantage once the agreement's details are made public.
Sensitive sectors including dairy, meat, poultry, maize, cereals, and genetically modified foods would remain protected, a February background paper published by India's Commerce Ministry said. The concessions include limited, reduced-duty import quotas for almonds, walnuts, and pistachios, while tariff reductions on certain other products would be phased in over up to ten years.
There would be zero additional US duties on selected Indian agricultural exports worth $1.36 billion, including tea, coffee, spices, and processed foods, according to the government.
The Samyukt Kisan Morcha, a coalition of more than 100 farmer organizations, has called for protests on November 26 and warned that subsidized American imports could depress domestic prices and hurt rural incomes. It has also demanded disclosure of the agreement's terms.
The All-India Kisan Sabha, another farmer organization, separately warned against opening up India's dairy market, arguing that cheaper US products could put pressure on milk procurement prices and rural households dependent on dairy farming.
Both Goyal and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio have said recently that the deal is near the finish line. However, some media reports have said talks have stalled as New Delhi refuses to accept a proposed 18% tariff rate along with concessions on farm products, and the final deal could come only after the November 3 US midterm elections.
